![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_13_fig_1.png)

Given triangle $ABC$ in figure 5 with $AB=12\,\text{cm}$ and $BC=5\,\text{cm}$.

figures.legende: Figure 5: triangle ABC with a right angle at B, AB = 12 cm and BC = 5 cm.

questions.corrige_markdown:
The right angle is at $B$, so $AC$ is the hypotenuse.

By Pythagoras: $AC^2=AB^2+BC^2=12^2+5^2=144+25=169$.

$AC=\sqrt{169}=13$ cm.

**$AC=13$ cm.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) angle $ACB$, to the nearest degree. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the right-angled triangle, relative to angle $C$: the opposite side is $AB=12$ and the adjacent side is $BC=5$.

$\tan(\angle ACB)=\dfrac{AB}{BC}=\dfrac{12}{5}=2.4$.

$\angle ACB=\tan^{-1}(2.4)\approx67.38^\circ$.

(Check with the hypotenuse: $\cos C=\dfrac{5}{13}$ gives the same angle.)

**$\angle ACB\approx67^\circ$ (to the nearest degree).**
